title: ID Churn Sentinel consumer watch map v1
description: A consumer-authored declaration of which published changes should become issues in THEIR repository, read by `consumer-action/raise_issues.py`. It lives in the consumer's repository and is never sent anywhere: this project holds no subscriber list, and this file is the subscription. Values are checked against the vocabulary carried by the fetched changes document itself, so a typo fails the run instead of matching nothing.

consumer.description: A name for your organization. Never sent anywhere; it is here so the file explains itself to the next person who opens it.

jurisdictions.description: Two-letter state codes, or `US` for the federal bucket. At least one of `jurisdictions` or `source_ids` must be present: a map with neither subscribes to every change in the country, which has to be written out rather than arrived at by omission.

document_classes.description: Which document classes you publish about, e.g. `drivers_license`. OMITTED means every class in the jurisdictions above — that is a deliberate widening, so it is spelled by leaving the key out rather than by an empty list.

source_ids.description: Specific sentinel source ids your pages cite. A change to one of these is always in scope, whatever the jurisdiction and class filters above say.

labels.description: Labels applied to every issue this action opens in your repository. They must already exist; this action creates no labels.
